text:
nina: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: release cadence, oncall handovers, and quality gates. Keeping this thread short for publishing.
carlos: Will we enforce a fixed 2-week release train across product teams or keep team-level flexibility?
zoe: And how are emergency hotfixes handled relative to the train?
nina: Target is a 2-week train for features; teams can still push low-risk fixes out-of-band if feature-flagged. Hotfixes follow an expedited path: oncall initial patch + release deputy sign-off within 60 minutes, then canary.
ops-bot: Expedited checklist: minimal diff, CI smoke, single-node canary, rollback instructions, post-deploy note.
carlos: Canary defaults and ramp policy? any differences for Dedicated customers?
nina: Default canary: 1% for 15m, then 10% for 15m, then full if healthy. Dedicated clusters may request slower ramps in customer config.
zoe: What are hard quality gates before production rollout?
nina: Must have green CI, no P99 regression >10% relative, <0.1% absolute increase in user 5xx, and a documented rollback plan.
carlos: Any change to oncall handover windows? we had confusion after the all-hands.
ops-bot: Handover window updated to 60 minutes; during launch weeks there will be a 2-hour overlap day.
zoe: Can you publish a one-page summary and calendar for the next two trains?
nina: Yes 1 Release ops will publish the summary and the release calendar by EOD tomorrow. Thanks, keep questions short here. :white_check_mark:
